metas.name: Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.note: Sugarcane plantations are very common in Northern Queensland, due to its tropical climate.

metas.name: Car Meta - Gen 3; Red Car; Long Antenna
metas.note: A red Generation 3 car with a long antenna can be seen in and east of Melbourne.

metas.name: Car Meta - Open Trunk Meta
metas.note: The town of Gascoyne Junction in Western Australia is distinct, as the driver left the car boot open while covering this town, creating a very unique car meta.

metas.name: Car Meta - Snorkel Car
metas.note:
Australia is home to dozens of rare Google cars, which can usually be found in natural reserves.

Most rare Google cars with snorkels are located in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory. The only snorkel cars outside of NSW are in the northwestern part of Wunaamin Conservation Area (northern WA) and along Lucky Bay (south coastal WA).

metas.name: Car Meta - Wire Car Meta
metas.note: On most of the Northern Territory section of the Barkly Highway and a small part of the Queensland section, a wire can be seen on the left side of the car.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Dirty Gen 2 Halo
metas.note: In some of New South Wales’ Generation 2, the halo looks very dirty. This is most common west of ACT and south of Barrington Tops.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Gen 2
metas.note: Generation 2 coverage cannot be found in Northern Territory. It can also help in 50/50s between Victoria and Tasmania, where Gen 2 is more common in Tasmania.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Gen 2 Twig Meta
metas.note: In Generation 2 coverage in an area of Eastern NSW, a twig is visible in the Generation 2 halo.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Gen 2 Whole Leaf
metas.note: In a lot of Generation 2 around the towns of Morwell and Traralgon in Eastern Victoria, an entire leaf is visible in the Generation 2 halo. A version with only the top half of a leaf can also be seen in eastern SA.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Half Leaf
metas.note: The upper half of a leaf can sometimes be seen on the Generation 2 halo in southeastern South Australia. If it's an entire leaf, it is in Eastern Victoria.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Jervis Bay Meta
metas.note: Jervis Bay only has Gen 1 coverage, all of which has a 2021 copyright.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Smoke Coverage
metas.note: Around the Devils Marbles, north of Davenport in the Northern Territory, smoke from a bushfire is visible.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Splodgey Sun
metas.note: A sun with "splodges" around it can be observed on the 95 in Western Australia, between Newman and Ex Doolgunna.
metas.footer: Published by zi8gzag on PlonkIt Discord

metas.name: Infrastructure - ∀-Poletop - Round
metas.note: The ∀-Poletop is found in South Australia and New South Wales. In SA, the pole will be a stobie pole, while in NSW it will be round.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - 130 km/h speed limit
metas.note: Within Australia, a speed limit of 130 km/h can only be found in the Northern Territory.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 25 school zone
metas.note: South Australia is the only Australian state that uses a 25 speed limit in school zones.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 90° poletop
metas.note: Poletops in Tasmania often consist of a thin metal crossbar bent 90 degrees to form an L-shape.

metas.name: Infrastructure - ACT Bus Stop
metas.note: Unique to Australian Capital Territory (Canberra).

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black pole marking
metas.note:
These black markings are specific to electricity poles in Queensland. They are often accompanied by diagonal numbers.

They are almost exclusively found between Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - black-white striped bollard
metas.note: These black-and-white stripy bollards are unique to Western Australia.

metas.name: Infrastructure - black-yellow striped bollard
metas.note: This black-and-yellow bollard is exclusive to Queensland.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Blue Square on Pole
metas.note: Melbourne poles commonly feature these white, rectangular stickers, with a smaller blue square inside it.

metas.name: Infrastructure - bollard with brown bottom
metas.note: Bollards with brown paint at the bottom are most commonly found in Western Australia.

metas.name: Infrastructure - bollard with short reflector
metas.note: Reflectors that are shorter than the regular ones are most common in Queensland and South Australia.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Brisbane Streetsign
metas.note: Identified by the little symbol.

metas.name: Infrastructure - C-Road
metas.note: Roads that start with the letter ‘C’ are only found in Victoria and Tasmania. In addition, South Australia has some C roads near the border with Victoria.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Charters Towers Red Roads
metas.note: As a general rule in Queensland state, Australia, red tinted roads are found mostly around Charters Towers (especially when you have more trees), they can also be found on the A2 near label, and the 1 further north. These areas are indicated in the distribution, but there may be minor exceptions.
metas.footer: Source: Meat of the Day on ScripterCord

metas.name: Infrastructure - concrete pole
metas.note: According to a 2006 review, 64% of all concrete poles are located in the state of Victoria.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Darwin Bus Stop
metas.note: The city of Darwin, NT uses concrete shelters as bus stops.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Dorat Road
metas.note: Dorat Road (23) in the Northern Territory can be easily recognized thanks to its distinct Darwin area landscape and lack of road lines.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Dotted Concrete Pole
metas.note: These round concrete poles with dots going up on them are found in New South Wales.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - flat signpost
metas.note: Some signposts in South Australia and Western Australia are flat rather than round.

metas.name: Infrastructure - fluoresecent sign border
metas.note: Road signs with a fluorescent border are almost exclusively found in Queensland.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Gold Coast Streetsign
metas.note: This street sign is unique to Gold Coast City Council.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Green Dot on Pole
metas.note: This Green Dot on poles is sometimes found in New South Wales.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - green pole bottom
metas.note: Poles in Western Australia often have green painted bases, and sometimes a white sticker or a red and white band attached.

metas.name: Infrastructure - green property marker
metas.note: You can find these dark green property markers on the sides of roads in Western Australia.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Hanging Insulator
metas.note: These poles with hanging insulators are found in Queensland and New South Wales.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - hydrant with blue circle
metas.note: You can find these white hydrant poles that feature a blue circle and a red section on top of it in Victoria.

metas.name: Infrastructure - hydrant with red top
metas.note: These fire hydrants with red painted tops are unique to Victoria.

metas.name: Infrastructure - License Plate - Slim NSW
metas.note: Very slim license plate (similar to Swiss front plates) are found in Victoria and New South Wales. While in Victoria, you can usually see two blue blocks of texts, in NSW they appear plain.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - License Plate - Slim Victoria
metas.note: Very slim license plate (similar to Swiss front plates) are found in Victoria and New South Wales. While in Victoria, you can usually see two blue blocks of texts, in NSW they appear plain.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - License Plate - Taxi - Blue
metas.note: Blue plates on Taxis are found exclusively in New South Wales.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - Mount Kosciuszko
metas.note:
All-yellow road lines can be seen on roads around Mount Kosciuszko.

In addition, a unique white truck with a snorkel, and cab guard can be found.

metas.name: Infrastructure - No-Stopping-sign with text
metas.note: The white ‘No Stopping’ and ‘No Parking’ signs that include text are unique to the Australian Capital Territory.

metas.name: Infrastructure - NSW Bus Stop
metas.note: New South Wales uses these two designs for bus stops. One is blue and has a white B in a circle with it, the other has the signpost bending over the actual sign.

metas.name: Infrastructure - NSW guardrail ending
metas.note: This guardrail ending, featuring a black dash on a yellow background, is almost exclusive to New South Wales and the ACT.

metas.name: Infrastructure - NT License Plate
metas.note: License Plates in Northern Territory have bright red lettering which shines through the blur. Looks kind of similar to the Queensland plates, which are a bit darker.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Octagonal Pole
metas.note: Octagonal Poles in Australia are found mostly in and around Sydney.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - olive-green possum guard
metas.note: Olive-green possum guards are only found on electricity poles in Tasmania.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Poletag - H
metas.note: The 'H' poletag is found in New South Wales.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - Poletag - HP
metas.note: This poletag with 'HP' is found in New South Wales.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - Poletag - NSW - Horizontal
metas.note: Within New South Wales, purely horizontal poletags (i.e. no vertical on the same pole), are not found around Sydney.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - Poletag - NSW - Letter Code
metas.note: In NSW, poletags in the triangle formed by Sydney, Newcastle and Scone (view map) almost always have one or two letters in their codes.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - Poletag - NSW - Vertical / Outer White
metas.note: Within NSW, these vertical plates with white ends are not found near Sydney. Note that otherwise, vertical plates will be close to Sydney within NSW.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - Poletag - QLD - Vertical
metas.note: Poletags with a blue sticker, and a vertical steel tag are found in Queensland, north of Rockhampton.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - Poletag - Vertical / Regular
metas.note:
Within NSW, regular vertical poletags are found south and west of Sydney.

Note that if the poletags have white ends on each side, they are NOT close to Sydney, but rather throughout the rest of NSW.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - Poletag - Yellow T
metas.note: This poletag which consists of rectangular yellow stickers that usually form a T, is exclusive to New South Wales.
metas.footer: Source: Australia Tips and Hints For Geoguessr - Definitive Edition by zi8gzag

metas.name: Infrastructure - Queensland Bus Stop
metas.note: Bus stops in Queensland have a yellow signpost bending over the actual sign.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Queensland License Plate
metas.note: The Queensland License Plate has dark red letters which can shine through the blur. Looks similar to the NT plate, which has a lighter red tone. There is also an old, green version, which could theoretically show up.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Queensland poletop
metas.note: Queensland features these unique pole tops with coils that are angled upwards on the sides.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Queensland sticker
metas.note: Circular blue stickers can be found on Queensland poles. You may occasionally see the same type of sticker in a different colour, or with the colour almost completely faded.

metas.name: Infrastructure - red "No Stopping" sign
metas.note: New South Wales is the only state to use red ‘No Stopping’ signs.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Roadline Gap with no Reflector
metas.note: In South Australia and the ACT, you can sometimes find gaps in the outer roadlines. If this gap has no reflector, it is South Australia.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt - Archived This meta was removed from the PlonkIt guide. The link leads you to the archived page.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Roadline gap with Reflector
metas.note: In South Australia and the ACT, you can sometimes find gaps in the outer roadlines. In ACT, there will always be a reflector in the gap. This can also appear occasionally in South Australia.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt - Archived This meta was removed from the PlonkIt guide. The link leads you to the archived page.

metas.name: Infrastructure - rusty holey pole
metas.note: These rusty metal poles, containing several holes, are unique to the Northern Territory, and rarely the northern part of Western Australia.

metas.name: Infrastructure - signpost with yellow sticker
metas.note: Signposts in the Northern Territory can feature these yellow stickers.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Sloped Kerbs
metas.note: You can sometimes see sloped kerbs in Perth, where it gradually declines to the road, whilst in other cities kerbs go straight down at a 90 degree angle.

metas.name: Infrastructure - South Australia Bus Stop
metas.note: Orange signpost, sign extending over the signpost.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Stobie pole
metas.note: The iconic Stobie pole, made of steel and concrete, is specific to South Australia. Outside of SA, it sometimes occurs in Broken Hill, NSW or Tasmania.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Sydney Streetsign
metas.note: This street sign is unique to the City of Sydney.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tasmania Bus Stop
metas.note: Different versions, but usually have "Metro" written on them.

metas.name: Infrastructure - thin "Keep Left" sign
metas.note: Some ‘Keep Left’ signs in New South Wales, Queensland, and the Northern Territory use this thinner version, which does not include an arrow.

metas.name: Infrastructure - traffic light with no outline
metas.note: Traffic lights without a border are found in Northern Territory, South Australia and Victoria.

metas.name: Infrastructure - traffic light with white outline
metas.note: Traffic lights with a white outline around the frame are found in the eastern and western states of WA, QLD, NSW, ACT and Tas. Traffic lights without a border are found in the remaining, central states.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Triple Broken Roadlines
metas.note: The Sturt Highway from Wentworth to Wagga Wagga can have triple broken centre lines. They can also be found on other major roads in NSW, such as the Gwydir Highway.

metas.name: Infrastructure - upward pointing trident pole
metas.note: A trident-like pole top with the insulators pointing to the top can sometimes be seen in Western Australia and Victoria.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Victoria Bus Stop
metas.note: Bus Stops in Victoria can be recognized by their color scheme: White-Orange-Black-Grey-White.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Victoria License Plate
metas.note: License plates in Victoria have a little small triangle at the top, which can sometimes be recognized through the blur.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Victoria poletop
metas.note: Victorian pole tops feature 3 circular coils; 2 on the sides, and 1 vertical one at the top. At times, other extensions can be seen on these poles.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Western Australia Bus Stop
metas.note: Bus Stops in Australia are marked by these horizontal poles with information on them.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Western Australia License Plate
metas.note: Western Australian License Plate have blue letters and a thin blue stripe at the top, which can sometimes be recognized through the blur.

metas.name: Infrastructure - white directional sign
metas.note: White directional signs can only be found in Tasmania.

metas.name: Infrastructure - white property marker
metas.note: You can find these white property markers on the sides of roads in South Australia.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Yellow License Plate
metas.note: Yellow license plates can occasionally be found in New South Wales. Most license plates are still white, though. The old design of Western Australian plates is also yellow, so you might stumble upon them in WA very rarely.

metas.name: Infrastructure - yellow signpost
metas.note: Yellow signposts are specific to Western Australia.

metas.name: Infrastructure - ш-shaped poletop
metas.note: Poletops that resemble the cyrillic letter ш are unique to South Australia.

metas.name: Landscape - Alice Springs
metas.note: Alice Springs, an isolated town in the southern part of the Northern Territory, features distinct orange rocks that can be seen in the distance or at the end of roads.

metas.name: Landscape - Cairns Landscape
metas.note: The northern QLD city of Cairns is distinct due to its tropical vegetation and big green mountains around the city.

metas.name: Landscape - Darwin Landscape
metas.note: The vegetation in the area surrounding Darwin is extremely distinct. It features dark red soil, as well as rich green grass and trees. The tree trunks are typically black.

metas.name: Landscape - Eastern South Australia Landscape
metas.note:
The dry area east of Adelaide and into northwestern Victoria has quite dry vegetation and is made up of shrubs and wide cronwed eucalyptus. In addition, the soil is sandy with a white tint.

Western South Australia has a similar landscape, but with orangish soil.

metas.name: Landscape - Green & Golden Fields
metas.note: Lush green or golden fields can be found in this band from the south of the Yorke Peninsula to Echuca. In the SA side, the landscape should be drier than the Victorian side and more wide crowned eucalyptus can be seen. On the Victorian side, the trees generally have more leaves and are taller.

metas.name: Landscape - Inland New South Wales Landscape
metas.note: The landscape in inland NSW is mostly flat, and the soil gets redder the more inland you go. Vegetation consists of mostly dry pale-green shrubs. Further east and on the Queensland and Victorian borders, the climate gets more temperate but is still quite dry and more eucalyptus trees can be seen, with the soil transitioning into a more sandy colour as well as more hills being visible.

metas.name: Landscape - Kangaroo Island Landscape
metas.note:
Kangaroo Island in South Australia tends to have a distinct look. The vegetation mostly consists of bushes and low, stubby eucalyptus trees with puffy clusters of leaves. The orange soil colour is reminiscent of Western Australia.

In addition, the island only has Generation 2 and Generation 4 coverage, with Generation 2 being most common.

metas.name: Landscape - Mount Gambier Tree Plantations
metas.note: The area around Mount Gambier, SA features white soil and extensive pine tree plantations, making it recognisable.

metas.name: Landscape - Northern Queensland Landscape
metas.note: Coastal northern Queensland is very tropical. Typical vegetation consists of palm trees and dark green vegetation.

metas.name: Landscape - Nullarbor Highway
metas.note:
The Nullarbor Highway (Latin for “no tree”) can be easily recognized thanks to the flatness, overall grey look and very low vegetation.

NOTE: Use the road angle or road lines to determine whether you are on the WA or SA side.

metas.name: Landscape - Reddish-Orange Soil
metas.note: Western Australia, and especially the Perth area, is known for its reddish-orange soil.

metas.name: Landscape - Stuart Highway with Blue Car
metas.note: The Stuart Highway from Alice Springs to around Pimba, SA can be easily recognized by its bright orange dirt, short trees and blue car Generation 4.

metas.name: Landscape - Tasmania Landscape
metas.note: Tasmania has a cool temperate climate which is uncommon in the rest of Australia and is comparable to central-southern Chile or New Zealand. Typical landscape consists of green rolling hills that can look dry in winter coverage. Eucalyptus trees can be seen on the side of roads and on hills in the distance. Rural Tasmania is also quite hilly with dense eucalyptus forests making up the landscape.

metas.name: Landscape - Termite Hills
metas.note: Termite mounds can sometimes be seen in the Northern Territory and rarely northern WA and QLD. They appear as brown, spiky formations rising out of the ground.

metas.name: Landscape - Tom Price Landscape
metas.note: The area around Tom Price can be recognized by its red soil and rocky hills.

metas.name: Landscape - Western South Australia Landscape
metas.note:
The area around Warramboo in SA to Madura in WA has a unique landscape. Vegetation is quite dry and is made up of shrubs and wide crowned eucalyptus. In addition, the soil is sandy with a slight orange tint.

The dry area east of Adelaide and into northwestern Victoria has a similar landscape, with the same vegetation but usually with whiter soil.

metas.name: Vegetation - Bottle Tree
metas.note: While Bottle Trees can be found throughout Queensland, they are planted everywhere in the city of Roma.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Meta Australia by trausi

metas.name: Vegetation - Brush Plant
metas.note: These brush plants are commonly seen in Western Australia.

metas.name: Vegetation - Gregory Tree
metas.note: Excoecaria parvifolia is an odd looking tree with almost creepy looking thin vine outgrowths as leaves. It seems to be found primarily found around the new 2025 white car coverage around the northern Queensland city of Gregory, Australia.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr: A Guide to Plants by gawynn1

metas.name: Vegetation - Queensland Fan Palm
metas.note: The Queensland fan palm or Australian fan palm, is a species endemic to northeastern Queensland, Australia (Specially around Cairns).
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Vegetation - Sand Palm
metas.note: The sand palm is endemic to the north of the Northern Territory of Australia, from the Fitzmaurice River to Cape Arnhem and inland as far as Katherine.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen
